name: Pickled fish
summary: Cape curried pickled fish (kerrievis): fried hake layered with onion rings in a sweet-sour curry vinegar sauce, made days ahead for Easter.
about: Pickled fish began as a Cape way of keeping the catch and is closely tied to Cape Malay cooking. Families make it before Good Friday and eat it over the Easter weekend, often with hot cross buns.
steps: Season the fish with the salt and turmeric, dust it in the flour and shake off the excess.

Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Fry the fish in batches for 2–3 minutes a side, until golden and just flaking. Drain on paper towel, then lay it in a single layer in a glass or ceramic dish (not metal, which reacts with vinegar).
In a stainless-steel or enamel saucepan, bring the vinegar, water, curry powder, turmeric, coriander seeds, peppercorns, bay leaves and salt to the boil over medium-high heat and boil for 2 minutes.
Add the onions and sugar and simmer on medium for 6–8 minutes, until the onions are tender but still have a little bite.
Stir in the cornflour paste and the jam and simmer for 1–2 minutes, until slightly thickened and glossy. Taste: it should be sharp and sweet at once; add a little sugar or vinegar to balance.
Pour the hot sauce and onions over the fish so it is covered. Cool, cover and refrigerate for at least 24 hours, and ideally 2–3 days.
Serve cold or at room temperature with buttered bread or hot cross buns. It keeps for 5 days in the fridge.
prepNote: Make it 2–3 days before you serve it; the flavour deepens. Keeps 5 days in the fridge.
